extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school and college administrators, legal counsel, and compliance officers responsible for implementing Title IX grievance procedures in educational institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for recipients (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions) to design and operate Title IX grievance procedures consistent with the Department's final regulations, including appeals, dismissal, consolidation, investigations, FERPA intersections, and supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer an appeal from a dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer an appeal from a dismissed complaint to the parties, consistent with the 2020 amendments; availability is conditioned on whether the respondent has been notified of the complaint and, once appealed, the same appeal procedures apply to both parties (§106.45(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(d)(3) to cross-reference §106.46(i)(1). The benefit of providing a review avenue justifies burdens on recipients. An appeal is considered necessary for dismissals because dismissal occurs before a determination and investigation may be initiated or completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted bases for appealing a dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from a dismissal may be made on the same bases required under the 2020 amendments: procedural irregularity; new evidence that was not reasonably available at the time of dismissal; or Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.45(d)(3) cross-references these bases at §106.46(i)(1). The Department clarified and retained these specific grounds for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for appeals and appeal outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify the complainant that a dismissal may be appealed and, if the dismissal occurs after the respondent was notified of the allegations, notify the respondent as well; if any party appeals, the recipient must notify all parties of the appeal and provide notice of the allegations consistent with §106.45(c) if needed; recipients must notify parties of the result of the appeal and the rationale for the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(d)(3)(i)–(vi) revised to separate notice and implementation requirements. For clarity, the Department replaced phrasing for consistency. The Department declines to require that the outcome be provided in writing but does not prohibit providing written notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on notifying respondents about appeal opportunity when they had no prior notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify the respondent that a dismissal may be appealed only if the dismissal occurs after the respondent has been notified of the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying a respondent of an appeal opportunity when they had no prior notice would likely cause confusion and would hinder the respondent's ability to meaningfully participate. If an appeal is filed and the respondent previously lacked notice, the recipient must provide notice of the allegations consistent with §106.45(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal implementation of appeal procedures once dismissal is appealed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a dismissal is appealed, the recipient must implement the same appeal procedures for all parties — provide notice when an appeal is filed, give a reasonable and equal opportunity to make statements supporting or challenging the outcome, and notify parties of the result and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department intentionally uses 'equal' in §106.45(d) to require identical appeal procedures for parties once an appeal proceeds; paragraph (d)(3)(v) requires equal opportunity to make statements and (d)(3)(vi) requires notification of the result and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest/bias prohibition for appeal decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker for an appeal must not have taken part in the investigation of the allegations or the dismissal of the complaint; e.g., the Title IX Coordinator is prohibited from deciding the appeal if they participated in the investigation or dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(d)(3)(iii) requires separation; §§106.45(b)(2) and 106.8(d)(2)(iii) further protect against bias and conflict of interest, including for appeal decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical requirement to provide written notice of appeal outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to notify parties in writing of the outcome of an appeal, recognizing stakeholder feedback that a written requirement can hinder prompt responses in elementary and secondary schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may still provide written notice voluntarily; nothing in the regulations prohibits complying with §106.45(d)(3)(vi) in writing. The Department balanced administrative burden on K–12 institutions against benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective steps after dismissal (supportive measures and prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complaint is dismissed, a recipient must, as appropriate, offer supportive measures to the complainant and, as applicable, the respondent, and take prompt and effective steps to ensure that sex discrimination does not continue or recur within its education program or activity (§106.45(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion to determine appropriate steps (e.g., convene a floor meeting retaining anonymity, encourage witnesses to come forward). §106.45(d)(4)(ii) requires equitable provision of supportive measures to respondents except where impracticable (unable to identify, not participating in program, or not notified). See §106.44(f)(1)(vii) for related discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient (institution) is responsible for complying with grievance procedures under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46; a Title IX Coordinator may delegate duties but must retain ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations permit delegation of specific duties to designees but the Title IX Coordinator retains ultimate oversight to ensure consistent compliance. The recipient, not the Coordinator alone, has the legal obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary consolidation of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may consolidate complaints (multiple complainants, multiple respondents, or one party against another) at their discretion; the Department declines to categorically require or prohibit consolidation and declines to specify detailed consolidation guidelines beyond §106.45(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider facts and circumstances, potential toll on parties, resources, fairness, and risks to investigation integrity. §106.45(e) guidance must be interpreted consistent with FERPA. §106.45(j) permits additional provisions so long as they apply equally to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections when consolidating (individual party rights and bias safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: When complaints are consolidated, each individual party retains every right granted under §§106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46; consolidation does not convert parties into a group and recipients must not weigh evidence differently due to consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators/decisionmakers must not have conflicts of interest or bias (§106.45(b)(2)); training on impartial service and avoiding prejudgment is required (§106.8(d)(2)(iii)). Recordkeeping documents training (§106.8(f)(1),(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation must comply with FERPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must interpret §106.45(e) consistently with FERPA and may not consolidate in a way that would violate FERPA's restrictions on disclosure of students' education records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is optional; if consolidation would cause a FERPA violation, the recipient must not consolidate. Recipients may obtain prior written consent to disclose records or redact irrelevant information while still complying with §106.45 and §106.46 obligations. FERPA exceptions for school officials with legitimate educational interest may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(f) requires recipients to provide for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigations of complaints — foundational to equitable adjudications and fair outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department highlights numerous procedural requirements across the regulations to support reaching adequate, reliable, and fair outcomes. §106.45(f) already states the impartiality requirement; §106.45(b)(1) and §106.45(b)(2) provide complementary obligations to ensure equitable treatment and absence of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative burden rests on the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients bear the burden to conduct investigations that gather sufficient evidence to determine whether sex discrimination occurred; recipients must not shift that burden to the parties or the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns about shifting burdens (e.g., affirmative consent policies). The Department affirms §106.45(f)(1) preserves recipient responsibility to investigate and gather evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators and decisionmakers must avoid bias and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or any individual party (§106.45(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(d)(2)(iii) mandates training on serving impartially and avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias. The Department leaves flexibility for additional bias training content beyond the mandated topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training content and flexibility for recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department requires certain training topics (including impartiality) but leaves recipients flexibility to choose additional content and substance beyond mandated topics (§106.8(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined §106.8(d) strikes a balance between mandating necessary topics to promote compliance and allowing maximum flexibility in training design. Nothing prevents recipients from providing training tailored to consolidated cases, multiple-respondent dynamics, or other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for grievance procedures and training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records documenting grievance procedures and the materials used to provide training (§106.8(f)(1) and (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining records supports accountability and demonstrates compliance with training and impartiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing witness credibility and investigation obligations remain when consolidating
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidation does not relieve a recipient of its obligations to conduct an adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation, including assessing witnesses' credibility to the extent it is in dispute and relevant (§106.45(f), (g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must still ensure fair investigations and compliance with §106.45 and §106.46 requirements, regardless of consolidation choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against retaliation including peer retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations prohibit harassment that amounts to retaliation, including peer retaliation; recipients must address retaliation even in consolidated cases (§106.2, §106.71).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a subsequent complaint is alleged to be retaliatory, the recipient must determine whether it constitutes prohibited retaliation under §106.71. Recipients must take steps to prevent and address retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution discretion and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(k), recipients have discretion to offer informal resolution, but may decline to offer it if the conduct alleged presents a future risk of harm; informal resolution agreements are binding only on participating parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should be mindful that informal resolution is optional and not appropriate in all cases. This discretion must be exercised consistent with other obligations under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of records when sharing evidence in consolidated complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may redact information that is not relevant to the allegations when sharing evidence, but when redacting they must still fully comply with §106.45 and §106.46 obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redaction cannot be used to circumvent procedural requirements. See related discussions of §§106.6(e), 106.45(b)(5), 106.45(f)(4), and 106.46(e)(6).
